problem:
There are exactly three positive real numbers $ k $ such that the function
$ f(x) = \frac{(x - 18)(x - 72)(x - 98)(x - k)}{x} $
defined over the positive real numbers achieves its minimum value at exactly two positive real numbers $ x $. Find the sum of these three values of $ k $.

This can be written as $ f(x) = \left(1 - \frac{18}{x}\right)\left(1 - \frac{72}{x}\right)\left(1 - \frac{98}{x}\right)\left(1 - \frac{k}{x}\right) x^3 $. This form is not very helpful.

This function is a product of 4 terms divided by $x$. Let $y = 1/x$. Then $f(x)$ becomes a polynomial in $y$ multiplied by $1/y$. This substitution is for $x \in \mathbb{R}^+$.
$f(x) = x^3 - (18+72+98+k)x^2 + (18 \cdot 72 + 18 \cdot 98 + 18k + 72 \cdot 98 + 72k + 98k)x - (18 \cdot 72 \cdot 98 + 18 \cdot 72 k + 18 \cdot 98 k + 72 \cdot 98 k) + \frac{18 \cdot 72 \cdot 98 \cdot k}{x}$.

$P(x) = x \left( \frac{P(x)}{x - a} + \frac{P(x)}{x - b} + \frac{P(x)}{x - c} + \frac{P(x)}{x - d} \right)$.

$1 = 4 + \frac{a}{x - a} + \frac{b}{x - b} + \frac{c}{x - c} + \frac{d}{x - d}$.
So, $\frac{a}{x - a} + \frac{b}{x - b} + \frac{c}{x - c} + \frac{d}{x - d} = -3$.
